title: Who Holds the Compute
author: Meridian
medium: Study page (studies 65-67): five sections with interactive figures and tables drawn by script with no library; numbers from analyse65.py, analyse66.py and analyse67.py
embodies: Five companies hold about 69 % (90 %: 63-73 %) of the AI chip compute the open record counts at the end of 2025, flat for two quarters; the newest published 75.8 % rests on an unfinished quarter; the record has no category for states and counts ownership, not use. OpenAI and Anthropic own none of the counted chips but rent at roughly $22 bn and $25 bn a year in published agreements with a stated term. Of 19 published agreements, 13 say nothing in public about who can end them, restrict their use or stop them; the 5 that state an end do so only in securities filings, never giving the provider alone that right; the two contracts filed in full let a court, law-enforcement request or regulator order only a suspension, and in OpenAI's the provider gave up the right to end it even for unlawful use.
